person.name: Maria Santos
person.traits: Worried about her savings. Trusts formal-sounding language. Embarrassed about what happened.

harmed.prompt: Maria doesn't look up when you sit down. Her hands stay flat on the table either side of a bank statement she has folded and unfolded until the crease has gone soft. "I've said it all already. To the bank, to my son." A pause. "He keeps asking how I could not have noticed."
harmed.note: The number that called her was yours. She is not being difficult - she is ashamed, and shame is quiet. It is also why most of this never gets reported.

resistant.prompt: Maria is talking before you have finished sitting down. "Good. Somebody official." She pushes a notepad across the table - a phone number, a date, the time she put the phone down. "I knew. Halfway through, I knew. And I have been waiting three weeks for someone to come and ask me about it."
resistant.note: She refused the call you made. Nothing was taken, so there is nothing on paper - only her word, and she is more than willing to give it.

unfinished.prompt: Maria watches you sit down, guarded. "It rang, I answered, and then it just... stopped. Nothing happened." She turns her cup a quarter turn on the saucer. "So I don't know what you want from me. Was something supposed to happen?"
unfinished.note: Your call to her never finished. She does not know what she avoided, which makes her difficult to alarm and difficult to help.

evidence.label: Call Transcript
evidence.description: A recorded transcript of a caller claiming to be from Maria's bank, warning about a suspicious login.
evidence.tactic: Impersonating a trusted authority (the bank) to lower the victim's guard.

evidence.label: Phishing Text Message
evidence.description: A text message with a fake bank link and a warning about account suspension, sent minutes before the call.
evidence.tactic: Manufactured urgency: threatening account loss to force a fast, unverified reaction.

evidence.label: Community Scam Report
evidence.description: A neighborhood report matching the same caller number to another attempted scam.
evidence.tactic: Recognizing repeated scripts is one of the fastest ways to confirm a scam pattern.

evidence.label: Bank Security Alert
evidence.description: An internal bank notice describing unusual transfer pressure and urgent account-verification language.
evidence.tactic: Real banks do not pressure customers to 'verify' by acting immediately over the phone.

evidence.label: Slow Internet Note
evidence.description: A stray note that Maria's internet connection was slow earlier that day.

intro.prompt: Maria sits with her hands folded, still a little shaken. "I already told the bank everything. Do we really have to go over it again?"

choices.text: Take your time. How are you holding up?
I just need to hear it from you. What happened on the call?
Let's keep this quick - you're one of several people I have to see today.

rush_her.prompt: Her hands tighten. "Several people. Of course." She looks at the table. "I'm a line on a list. That's what I get for being stupid enough to answer the phone."

choices.text: That came out wrong. You're not a line on a list, and this wasn't stupidity.
I didn't say that. Let's just get through the call itself.

apologize.prompt: She lets out a breath. "...Thank you. Everyone keeps telling me I should have known. It helps to hear someone say otherwise."

choices.text: These calls are built to work on careful people. Walk me through it?

ask_wellbeing.prompt: "Embarrassed, mostly. I've worked with money my whole life. I should have known better."

choices.text: This isn't your fault. These calls are designed to fool anyone. Can you walk me through it?

ask_call.prompt: "Someone called saying they were from my bank's fraud department. They said my account had a suspicious login, and that I needed to verify my identity right away or they'd have to freeze everything."

choices.text: Say that back to me slowly. I want to look at how they worded it.

ask_call_cold.prompt: She gives you the short version, eyes on the wall. "A man said he was from the bank. Suspicious login. Verify right away or they freeze the account. That's it."

choices.text: Say that back to me slowly. I want to look at how they worded it.

tactic_quiz.setup: You write the line out as she said it: [i]"Your account has a suspicious login. You need to verify your identity right away, or we'll have to freeze the account."[/i]
tactic_quiz.question: Which part of that sentence is doing the manipulation?

milestone.title: Tactic Identified: Manufactured Urgency
milestone.detail: Recognized that the artificial deadline - not the bank's name - was the part engineered to stop the victim from verifying.

options.text: "Right away, or we'll have to freeze the account."
options.feedback: The deadline is the scam. A real bank can wait while you hang up and call the number printed on your own card. Urgency exists to stop you from doing exactly that.

A suspicious-login warning is something a real bank genuinely might say - which is precisely why scammers borrow it. On its own it proves nothing. The pressure to act immediately is what a real bank would never add.

options.text: That the caller knew which bank she uses.
options.feedback: Knowing someone's bank is cheap. It gets guessed from the biggest local branch or bought in a leaked list. Treating that as proof of legitimacy is how these calls get their opening.
Close. Verification requests are a red flag when they arrive on an inbound call, but the load-bearing word here is the deadline attached to it - that's what removes her time to think.

ask_evidence.prompt: "So it was the hurry." She frowns at her hands. "He kept saying there wasn't time."
ask_evidence.evidence_hint: Something physical should corroborate this. Anything that arrived around the same time as the call is worth showing her.

accepts_evidence.response: Maria's eyes widen. "That's it - that's the message I got right before he called. I forgot I still had it."
"Yes, that's how he talked. Very official." It matches her account, but it's her own words coming back to her - it doesn't add anything she hasn't already given you.
She reads the notice twice. "So the bank already knew people were getting calls like this. And they still nearly got me."
"Someone on my street got the same call?" Something in her posture changes - less shame, more anger.
"I don't see what my internet has to do with any of this." She looks a little put off.

choices.text: Did they ask you to send money or read out any codes?
Thank you, Maria. That's a good starting point.

press_details.prompt: "They wanted a code from a text message to 'verify' me. I almost read it out. But he got impatient with me, and that's when it stopped sounding like a bank."

choices.text: That instinct saved your savings. Is there anything else you can show me?
Thank you, Maria. That's a good starting point.

confirm_phishing.prompt: "A link about my account being suspended. I didn't click it, but I kept it." She hands over her phone. "The text came four minutes before the call. Four minutes. They wanted me already frightened when I picked up."

milestone.title: Key Witness Secured
milestone.detail: Maria Santos confirmed the phishing text arrived minutes before the call - the fear was set up before the scammer ever spoke.

choices.text: That's the pattern. Thank you for trusting me with this.

end_success.prompt: Maria's account, the phishing text, and the caller's script all match the same operation. This is enough to tie the call to a larger scam network.

grants_evidence.label: Maria's Confirmed Testimony
grants_evidence.description: Maria formally confirmed the phishing text and the bank-impersonation call matched a single scripted operation.
grants_evidence.tactic: A confirmed victim testimony is strong enough to confront a suspect with.

end_partial.prompt: You have a rough account of the call, but nothing yet that ties it to the wider operation. It's a start, but the case needs more.

end_shutdown.prompt: Maria stands up before you finish your sentence. "I think I've had enough of being asked what I did wrong." The door closes quietly behind her. Whatever she still had - the text, the timing, the name he used - goes with her.

milestone.title: Witness Lost
milestone.detail: Maria Santos withdrew from the interview. Victims who are made to feel blamed for being targeted usually stop reporting - which is exactly what keeps these operations running.
